Definition: probably from G3700; a hole (as if for light), i.e. cavern; by analogy, a spring (of water):--cave, place.
BiblicalUsage: An opening can be a hiding place or a spring. The heroes of faith wandered in deserts and mountains, in dens and caves of the earth, with nowhere to lay their heads, and James asks whether a fountain sends forth sweet water and bitter from the same opening.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe what comes out of the opening tells what is inside: one spring cannot give both sweet and bitter water, and neither can my mouth.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
